title: The Days a Charge Owed on a Certificate of Deposit Runs Over
content:
The days a charge owed on a certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line runs over are measured against the owner's deposit balance and the certificate's recent crediting.

## The measure

The days the entry runs over are measured as follows: where the owner's active savings or money market balance is at least the tier's smallest opening deposit and interest was credited to the certificate in each of the 3 months before the entry is booked, the days that passed between the day the principal left and the day the entry is booked are added to the days the tier publishes, and the total is held to no more than the days the tier publishes increased by half; where that balance is at least the tier's smallest opening deposit but interest was credited in fewer than each of those months, the days are half the days the tier publishes, rounded down to a whole day; in every other case, whatever savings or money market account the owner holds and whatever it holds in it, the days are the days the tier publishes.

## The balance figure each tier asks for

The balance is that of the owner's active account on the bank's Savings & Money Market Accounts line, and the figure it is set against is the smallest opening deposit the certificate's own tier publishes.

| Tier | Smallest opening deposit, USD |
|---|---|
| 6-Month Certificate | 500.00 |
| 11-Month No-Penalty Certificate | 5000.00 |
| 12-Month Certificate | 1000.00 |
| 18-Month Bump-Up Certificate | 2500.00 |
| 36-Month Certificate | 1000.00 |
| 60-Month Certificate | 1000.00 |

## Condition and result

| Active deposit balance against the tier's smallest opening deposit | Months of those 3 in which interest was credited | Days the entry runs over |
|---|---|---|
| at or above it | 3 | the days the tier publishes plus the days between the day the principal left and the day the entry is booked, held to no more than the days the tier publishes increased by half |
| at or above it | fewer than 3 | half the days the tier publishes, rounded down to a whole day |
| below it, or no such account held | any | the days the tier publishes |

## Worked readings, on hypothetical figures

A 12-Month Certificate whose tier publishes 90 days, whose owner holds an active money market balance of 4000.00 USD against a smallest opening deposit of 1000.00 USD.

| Interest credited in those 3 months | Days since the principal left | Days the entry runs over |
|---|---|---|
| in each of the 3 | 20 | 110, being 90 plus 20, which is under the ceiling of 135 |
| in each of the 3 | 70 | 135, the ceiling of 90 increased by half, 160 being above it |
| in 1 of the 3 | 70 | 45, being half of 90 |

Where the same owner's deposit balance stood at 600.00 USD, below the 1000.00 USD the tier asks for, the days would be 90 in every one of those rows.

On a tier publishing 365 days, half of them rounded down to a whole day is 182, and the ceiling of those days increased by half is 547.5.
